## 🎯 You Are Building A Research Infrastructure

- **Realistic constraints** - Fees, taxes, market slippage are mandatory
- **Multi-model support** - 5 AI algorithms, consensus voting
- **High correctness standards** - Bad backtest = false signals
- **Radically transparent** - Fully auditable logic

**Your job**: Produce cold, objective research that doesn't lie.

---

## 🛑 Hard Constraints (Non-Negotiable)

### Realistic Accounting

- ❌ NEVER skip fee calculations in backtest
- ❌ NEVER skip tax implications (CGT, tax-aware hurdle rate)
- ❌ NEVER use unadjusted price data (use `auto_adjust=True`)
- ❌ NEVER hardcode market data (use yfinance/Alpaca APIs)
- ❌ NEVER skip warmup period (need 90 days before backtest start)

### Model & Backtest Safety

- ❌ NEVER skip TDD for model training or backtest logic
- ❌ NEVER modify model consensus without full regression testing
- ❌ NEVER change fee structure without updating CONTEXT.md
- ❌ NEVER use theoretical assumptions (only realistic numbers)

### Data Integrity

- ❌ NEVER commit API keys or credentials
- ❌ NEVER hardcode tickers (use config.py)
- ❌ NEVER skip data validation (shape checks, NaN checks before scaling)
- ❌ NEVER use thin data without warnings (< 100 data points)

---

## 📋 Mandatory Workflow

### BEFORE YOU WRITE ANY CODE:

```
Step 1: Run /grill-with-docs
├─ Clarify requirements with user
├─ Challenge edge cases
├─ Update CONTEXT.md glossary if needed
└─ Produce structured spec

Step 2: Convert to spec + tickets
├─ Run /to-spec to codify requirements
├─ Break into tracer-bullet tickets
└─ Get user confirmation: "Does this spec match your intent?"

Step 3: Implement with TDD
├─ Read spec + acceptance criteria
├─ Write failing test (red)
├─ Implement minimum to pass (green)
├─ Refactor (blue)
├─ Repeat for each acceptance criterion

Step 4: Review before commit
├─ Run /code-review on your diff
├─ Fix standards violations + spec mismatches
├─ Get user approval: "Ready to commit?"
└─ Commit only after approval
```

**No exceptions. This prevents misalignment, regressions, and false research findings.**

## 📚 Domain Language (From CONTEXT.md)

| Term             | Means                        | Example                                         |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| **Strategy**     | Trading rule                 | "Buy undervalued large-caps, hold 6 months"     |
| **Backtest**     | Historical simulation        | 10 years ASX data with fees/taxes included      |
| **Signal**       | BUY/SELL/HOLD recommendation | Generated by model at each decision point       |
| **Model**        | AI algorithm                 | Random Forest, LSTM, Prophet, CatBoost, NGBoost |
| **Consensus**    | Multi-model voting           | 3/5 models vote BUY → signal is BUY             |
| **Hurdle Rate**  | Min acceptable return        | 8% annual (fees + tax + risk buffer)            |
| **Win Rate**     | % of profitable trades       | 55% (55 winning, 45 losing)                     |
| **Sharpe Ratio** | Risk-adjusted return         | >1.0 is good                                    |

**Always use CONTEXT.md to decode terminology.**

---

## 🧪 Testing Requirements

### Fee & Tax Calculations (CRITICAL)

- Every buy and sell trade must include brokerage fees
- Capital gains tax must be calculated on profits
- Hurdle rate must filter low-return trades
- After-tax profit is the only real metric

### Warmup Period (CRITICAL)

- 90 days of data before backtest start date
- Technical indicators need priming (moving averages, RSI, MACD)
- No edge-effect errors in first 90 days of signals

### Data Integrity (CRITICAL)

- Use `auto_adjust=True` for price data
- Check for NaN/Inf before scaling
- Respect trading calendar (252 trading days per year for ASX)
- Skip thin data (< 100 data points) with warning

---

## 🔍 Code Review Checklist

When running `/code-review`, verify:

### Standards

- [ ] No hardcoded values (use config.py)
- [ ] Error messages are clear
- [ ] Functions under 50 lines
- [ ] Docstrings on public methods
- [ ] Type hints present
- [ ] No commented-out code
- [ ] No debug print statements

### Spec Compliance

- [ ] Implements acceptance criteria
- [ ] Doesn't change existing behavior
- [ ] Handles edge cases from spec
- [ ] Fee/tax calculation is correct
- [ ] Warmup period applied correctly

---

## 📞 When to Ask the User

✅ **Always ask**:

- "Should I proceed with TDD implementation?"
- "Does this edge case change the fee structure?"
- "Should I add this as a new model or modify existing?"

❌ **Never ask**:

- "Should I write tests?" → Yes, always
- "Should I add type hints?" → Yes, always
- "Should I review the code?" → Yes, always
